recon.notes: Recon from one live read of each door on 2026-10-18. The promoter runs two weekends a year — Urban Bear NYC in September and Fire Island Bear Weekend in June — and the site is the schedule of each, rewritten in place for the next edition; on the recon date both pages still carried the 2026 editions, four weeks and four months past. Bear World Magazine and Gathr carried 16 copies of these nights as aggregators; this is the promoter's own statement. Nights are co-produced with the venues (Rockbar, Nowhere Bar, Ty's, Julius', FLEX) whose own parsers may also publish them.

coverage.basis: Every dated statement on both pages the site's nav offers is in the past on 2026-10-18 — Urban Bear NYC, September 17–20, 2026 (8 nights on the home page) and Fire Island Bear Weekend, June 11–15, 2026 (12 entries on /fibw) — and the configured page's ?format=json twin is a plain page with itemCount 0, so no collection holds anything else. The 2027 dates are not announced. Past listings: 20 schedule entries across the two pages, counted not enumerated.

traps.why: A promoter's root may link its ticketing platform, so same-depth outbound links are followed; here they lead to the sponsors' own sites. Rockbar's home page carries an Elfsight calendar and the Elfsight reader opened it inside this parser's crawl: 107 of the run's 128 records are Rockbar's nights (ARCADE, ORAL EXAM TRIVIA, GORDITOS, BEARS NIGHT OUT, PEEP SHOW…), each stamped bear by the promoter's bearAffinity and given https://www.theurbanbear.com as website by the registry identity; The Standard's /specials page yielded "Sunday Views" (2027-01-06) and "Frieze London" (city london). Rockbar has its own parser; none of this is Urban Bear's programming and none of it belongs under this source.
traps.note: Live requests in that run: 36 to 19 hosts (eventbrite.com 2, reflectionsfip.com 2, standardhotels.com 2, hyatt.com parked on 403, paypal.me refused by robots). The generic question — may a platform door (Elfsight, Squarespace twin, Wix blob, DICE, MEC) open on a host outside the source's configured domain, and may a registry identity rewrite the website of records read off another org's site — is raised in openQuestions and left to the owner; no per-site block was added.

openQuestions.q: Run 20261018-114836: the crawl followed the home page's sponsor links to rockbarnyc.com and read Rockbar's Elfsight calendar as 107 Urban Bear events (bear by bearAffinity, website rewritten to theurbanbear.com by the registry identity). Proposed generic rule, not built: a platform door opened on a page whose registrable domain is not one of the source's configured domains yields nothing for that source (the host's own parser owns it), and the registry identity never overwrites a website that points at another configured source's domain. Owner decision — it changes crawl semantics for every promoter root that links its venues. — Resolved 2026-10-18: the stanza sets discoveryAllowedPatterns ["theurbanbear.com"], so discovery never leaves the promoter's own pages; the crawl-policy question (platform doors on hosts outside a source's domains) stays open as a generic concern.

Fire Island Bear Weekend's venues (Cherry’s on the Bay, The Belvedere, The Pines Pavilion, Reflections, The Blue Whale, The Tryst Pool Club) have no curated data/bars/fire-island.json; the site prints one street address (Reflections, 73 Bay Walk) and no coordinates, so none could be added with justified coordinates. Owner call before the June 2027 edition.

The weekend passes are Eventbrite pages (a cc/ collection for NYC, an /e/ event for FIBW) with structured dates; whether to follow them as doors is open — the schedule text is the fuller statement (per-night venue, hour, price).

scraper-cities' hong-kong patterns include the bare token "hk"; "FLEX HK" (Hell's Kitchen) resolved to hong-kong in run 20261018-114836 although the block prints a Manhattan street address. Dropping "hk" or requiring a longer match is a one-line data change with cross-city consequences — owner call.
